old_digest: One wicket shall be pitched, as in Law 6, with a bowling stump opposite to it, at a distance of 22 yards. The bowling crease shall be in a line with the bowling stump, and drawn according to Law 7.
new_digest: One wicket shall be pitched, as in Law 6, with a bowling stump opposite to it, at a distance of 22 yards. The bowling crease shall be in line with the bowling stump, and drawn according to Law 7.

old_digest: There shall be no restriction as to the ball being bowled in overs, but no more than one minute shall be allowed between each ball.
new_digest: There shall be no restriction as to the ball being bowled in overs, but no more than one minute shall be allowed between each ball.

old_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed 22 yards each in a line from the off and leg stump.
new_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed 22 yards each in a line from the off and leg stump.

old_digest: The ball must be hit before the bounds to entitle the striker to a run, which run cannot be obtained unless he touch the bowling stump or crease in a line with his bat, or some part of his person, or go beyond them, and return to the popping crease.
new_digest: The ball must be hit before the bounds to entitle the striker to a run, which run cannot be obtained unless he touch the bowling stump or crease in a line with his bat, or some part of his person, or go beyond them, and return to the popping crease.

old_digest: When the striker shall hit the ball, one of his feet must be on the ground behind the popping crease, otherwise the umpire shall call “No hit,” and no run shall be scored.
new_digest: When the striker shall hit the ball, one of his feet must be on the ground, behind the popping crease, otherwise the umpire shall call “no hit,” and no run shall be scored.

old_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, neither byes, leg-byes, nor overthrows shall be allowed, nor shall the striker be caught out behind the wicket, nor stumped.
new_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, neither byes, leg-byes, nor overthrows shall be allowed, nor shall the striker be caught out behind the wicket, nor stumped.

old_digest: The fieldsman must return the ball so that it shall cross the ground between the wicket and the bowling stump, or between the bowling stump and the bounds; the striker may run till the ball be so returned.
new_digest: The fieldsman must return the ball so that it shall cross the ground between the wicket and the bowling stump, or between the bowling stump and the bounds.

old_digest: After the striker shall have made one run, if he start again he must touch the bowling stump or crease and turn before the ball cross the ground to entitle him to another.
new_digest: After the striker shall have made one run, if he starts again he must touch the middle stump or crease, and turn before the ball cross the ground to entitle him to another.

old_digest: The striker shall be entitled to three runs for lost ball, and the same number for ball wilfully stopped by a fieldsman otherwise than with any part of his person.
new_digest: The striker shall be entitled to three runs for lost ball, and the same number for ball wilfully stopped by a field-man otherwise than with any part of his person.

old_digest: When there shall be more than four players on a side there shall be no bounds. All hits, byes, leg-byes, and overthrows shall then be allowed.
new_digest: When there shall be more than four players on a side there shall be no bounds. All runs, byes, leg byes, and overthrows shall then be allowed.

old_digest: The side which goes in second shall follow their innings if they have scored 60 runs less than the opposite side.
new_digest: The side which goes in second shall follow their innings if they have scored 75 runs less than the opposite side.

old_digest: Prior to the commencement of a match it may be agreed that the over consists of 5 or 6 balls.
new_digest: Prior to the commencement of a match it may be agreed that the over consist of five or six balls.

old_digest: One wicket shall be pitched, as in Law 6, with a bowling stump opposite to it, at a distance of 22 yards. The bowling crease shall be in a line with the bowling stump, and drawn according to Law 7. When there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed 22 yards each in a line from the off and leg stump. The ball must be hit before the bounds to entitle the striker to a run, which run cannot be obtained unless he touch the bowling stump or crease in a line with his bat, or some part of his person, or go beyond them, and return to the popping crease. A match is played between two sides of eleven players each, unless otherwise agreed to; each side has two innings, taken alternately, except in the case provided for in Law 53.
new_digest: A match is played between two sides of 11 players each, unless otherwise agreed to. Each side has two innings, taken alternately, except in the case provided for in Law 53.

old_digest: The ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked, the umpire shall call “No ball.”
new_digest: The ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked either umpire shall call “no ball.”

old_digest: The ball shall be bowled in overs of five balls from each wicket alternately. When five balls have been bowled, and the ball is finally settled in the bowler’s or wicket-keeper’s hands, the umpire shall call “Over.” Neither a “no-ball” nor a “wide-ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “over.”
new_digest: The ball shall be bowled in overs of six balls from each wicket alternately. When six balls have been bowled, and the ball is finally settled in the bowler's or wicket-keeper’s hands, the umpire shall call “over.” Neither a “no ball” nor a “wide ball” shall be reckoned as one of the over.

old_digest: The bowler shall be allowed to change ends as often as he pleases, provided only that he does not bowl two overs consecutively in one innings.
new_digest: The bowler may change ends as often as he pleases, provided that he shall not bowl two overs in succession in the same innings.

law_title: SCORING OFF NO BALLS AND WIDE BALLS
old_digest: The striker may hit a “no-ball,” and whatever runs result shall be added to his score; but he shall not be out from a “no-ball,” unless he be run out or break laws 26, 27, 29, 30. All runs made from a “no-ball,” otherwise than from the bat, shall be scored “no-balls,” and if no runs be made one run shall be added to that score. From a “wide-ball” as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as “wide balls,” and if no runs be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.
new_digest: The striker may hit a “no ball,” and whatever runs result shall be added to his score; but he shall not be out from a “no ball” unless he be run out or break Laws 26, 27, 29 and 30. All runs made from a “no ball,” otherwise than from the bat, shall be scored “no balls,” and, if no run be made, one run shall be added to that score. From a “wide ball” as many runs as are run shall be added to that score as “wide balls,” and if no runs be otherwise obtained, one run shall be so added.

old_digest: 1st So often as the batsmen after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end; 2nd For penalties under Laws 16, 34, 41, and allowances under 44.
new_digest: A run is scored:— 1.—So often as the batsman after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed and made good their ground from end to end. 2.—For penalties under Laws 16, 34, 41, and allowances under 41.

old_digest: If the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the striker’s bat or person :—“Bowled.”
new_digest: The striker is out if the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the striker's bat or person:

old_digest: If in running, or at any other time, while the ball is in play, he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm, with ball in hand, of any fieldsman:—“Run out.”
new_digest: Either batsman is out if in running, or at any other time, while the ball is in play, he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm (with ball in hand) of any fieldsman:—“Run out.”

old_digest: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any fieldsman may call “lost ball,” when the ball shall be “dead”; six runs shall be added to the score, but if more than six runs have been run before “lost ball” has been called, as many runs as have been run shall be scored.
new_digest: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any fieldsman may call “lost-ball,” when the ball shall be “dead;” six runs shall be added to the score; but if more than six runs have been run before “lost ball” has been called as many runs as have been run shall be scored.

old_digest: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the wicket-keeper’s or bowler’s hand it shall be “dead”; but when the bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said bowler may run him out; but if the bowler throw at that wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “no-ball.”
new_digest: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the wicket keeper’s or bowler's hand, it shall be ‘dead;” but when the bowler is about to deliver the ball if the batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said bowler may run him out; but if the bowler throw at the wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “no ball.”

old_digest: The ball shall weigh not less than 5½oz. nor more than 5¾oz. It shall measure not less than 9in. nor more than 9½in. in circumference.
new_digest: The ball shall weigh not less than five ounces and a half, nor more than five ounces and three-quarters. It shall measure not less than nine inches, nor more than nine inches and one quarter in circumference.

old_digest: A batsman is liable to be out for any infringement of the laws by his substitute.
new_digest: A batsman is liable to be put out for any infringe ment of the laws by his substitute.

old_digest: The fieldsman may stop the ball with any part of his person, but if he wilfully stop it otherwise the ball shall be “dead,” and five runs added to the score. Whatever runs may have been made five only shall be added.
new_digest: The fieldsman may stop the ball with any part of his person, but if he wilfully stop it otherwise, the ball shall be “dead” and five runs added to the score; whatever runs may have been made, five only shall be added.

old_digest: When they shall call “Play,” the side refusing to play shall lose the match.
new_digest: When they call “play” the side refusing to play shall lose the match.

old_digest: If the umpire at the bowler’s end be not satisfied of the absolute fairness of the delivery of any ball, he shall call “No ball.” 48½.
new_digest: If either umpire be not satisfied of the absolute fairness of the delivery of any ball, he shall call “no ball.”
The umpire shall take special care to call “no ball” instantly upon delivery; “wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.

old_digest: The umpire shall take especial care to call “No ball” instantly upon delivery, “Wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.
new_digest: The umpire shall take special care to call “no ball” instantly upon delivery; “wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.

old_digest: The bat shall not exceed 4¼in. in the widest part; it shall not be more than 38in. in length.
new_digest: The bat shall not exceed four inches and one-quarter in the widest part; it shall not be more than 38 inches in length.

old_digest: No umpire shall be changed during a match unless with the consent of both sides, except in case of violation of Law 51, then either side may dismiss him.
new_digest: No umpire shall be changed during a match unless with the consent of both sides, except in case of violation of Law 51, when either side may dismiss him.

old_digest: The side which goes in second shall follow their innings, if they have scored 120 runs less than the opposite side in a threedays match, or 80 runs in a two-days match.
new_digest: The side which goes in second shall follow their innings if they have scored 150 runs less than the opposite side. 1.—On the last day of a match, or if a one day match at any time, the in-side shall be empowered to declare the innings at an end.

old_digest: On the last day of a match, or if a one-day match, at any time, the in-side shall be empowered to declare the innings at an end.

Each wicket shall be 8in. in width, and consist of three stumps, with two bails upon the top. The bails shall be each 4¼in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them.
new_digest: Each wicket shall be eight inches in width, and consist of three stumps, with two bails upon the top. The bails shall be each four inches in length, and, when in position on top of the stumps, shall not project more than half-an-inch above them.

old_digest: The bowling crease shall be in a line with the stumps, 6ft. 8in. in length; the stumps in the centre, with a return crease at each end, at right angles behind the wicket.
new_digest: The bowling crease shall be in a line with the stumps 6 feet 8 inches in length, the stumps in the centre, with a return crease at each end, at right angles behind the wicket.

old_digest: The popping crease shall be marked 4ft. from the wicket, parallel to it, and be deemed unlimited in length.
new_digest: The popping crease shall be marked four feet from the wicket, parallel to it, and deemed unlimited in length.
